args.note: AGC subroutines have no formal parameter list (why_gitgalaxy_beats_ast_here.md Claim 1's shape) -- args is a real body-idiom proxy: the number of DISTINCT accumulator-style registers (A/Q/L/Z) a function's body demonstrably reads via a real math/memory opcode, plus one more if an EBANK=/FBANK=/BBANK= bank-context assignment is present. Fixed in gitgalaxy/core/detector.py's new _count_agc_register_args (#1949 follow-up) to scan every match in the body (findall) instead of deriving from only the first regex match (search-then-split), which previously produced a near-meaningless 0/1/2 categorical value regardless of how many registers a function actually touched. Spot-checked by hand against direct source reading for 5 functions across 4 different corpus files (P40AUTO=1 register A, TESTBIT=1 register A via CCS A before a TC Q early-return truncates the rest, SMODECHK=0 no coupled-register opcode present, KILLTASK=3 registers A+Q plus an EBANK= bank assignment, CGCALC=3 registers A+L plus an EBANK= bank assignment) -- zero discrepancies found. Total is the sum of every real function's own distinct-register-plus-bank-flag count across the corpus, computed via the same struct_func_start/function_data pipeline path abap's own args entry uses. ctags emits no signature: field for Asm-parsed files, so no second tool can ever corroborate this metric -- confirmed via `ctags --fields=+S`, same structural limitation as the whole-language 1-tool case, scoped here to just the args metric (agc_assembly has real ctags coverage for func/class existence).

Per-function declared-parameter count, spot-checked against direct source reading for 9 functions across 4 different corpus files (constructor, create_empty, create_from, build_asx_node, parse, push, serialize, deserialize, deserialize_checks) after fixing #1917 (args regex correctness) and #1918 (DEFINITION-section span lookup + dedicated counter, gitgalaxy/core/detector.py's _count_abap_declared_params) -- zero discrepancies found. Total is the sum of every real function's own args count across the corpus, not a per-clause or per-file signal count (distinct from the file-level struct_args structural signature).

class.note: class_start regex applied directly to source text, cross-checked against every real CLASS DEFINITION/IMPLEMENTATION pair in the corpus by direct reading -- see docs/language_status/abap.md §9.

function.note: func_start regex applied directly to source text, cross-checked against an independent grep (grep -nE "^\s*METHOD\s+[a-zA-Z]") that shares no implementation with the primary regex -- see docs/language_status/abap.md §9.
